law_name: Oslo Accords: Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government Arrangements (Oslo I, 1993) and Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip (Oslo II, 1995)
description: Abbas, who according to Britannica shaped the PLO's strategy in the secret talks in Norway, signed the Declaration of Principles for the PLO on the White House lawn on 13 September 1993, and according to his official biography also signed the Oslo II interim agreement in Washington in September 1995. Under the accords Israel and the PLO recognised each other and Israel transferred some governing functions in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to the new Palestinian Authority.
significance: Created the Palestinian Authority he would later lead. In September 2015 he told the UN General Assembly that the Palestinians were no longer bound by the accords, accusing Israel of repeatedly violating them, though without naming concrete steps (Britannica).

law_name: Decree-Law No. 1 of 2007 on General Elections
description: Issued by decree in September 2007, after the June 2007 split with Hamas, while the Legislative Council could not convene; it replaced the mixed system used in 2006 (half the seats by lists, half by districts) with full proportional representation. Hamas, which held a majority in the Legislative Council, called the change illegal.
significance: Remains the framework for Palestinian general elections; amended by decree-law in June 2026 (see below).

law_name: UN General Assembly Resolution 67/19: non-member observer state status for Palestine
description: After his September 2011 request for full UN membership stalled in the Security Council, Abbas submitted a draft resolution upgrading Palestine's status from 'permanent observer' entity to 'non-member observer state'. It passed on 29 November 2012 by 138 votes to 9, with 41 abstentions, over the opposition of Israel and the United States.
significance: Gave the State of Palestine access to international treaties and bodies, including the International Criminal Court; the PA has since used the name 'State of Palestine' for all purposes.

law_name: Accession of the State of Palestine to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
description: Abbas signed the application to join the ICC in December 2014, one day after the UN Security Council rejected a resolution demanding an end to the Israeli occupation and Palestinian statehood by 2017; the State of Palestine was admitted to the Court in April 2015.
significance: Gave the State of Palestine standing before the Court. The United States cited the PA's actions at the ICC and the International Court of Justice among its reasons for visa sanctions on PLO and PA officials in 2025 and 2026.

law_name: Dissolution of the Palestinian Legislative Council (Supreme Constitutional Court ruling announced by Abbas)
description: On 22 December 2018 Abbas told the Palestinian leadership that the Supreme Constitutional Court had issued a decision dissolving the Hamas-majority Legislative Council, which had not met since 2007, and calling legislative elections within six months; he said the leadership would abide by it (WAFA, via Arab News).
significance: Critics, including the editor of the Palestine Yearbook of International Law, called it a political rather than legal decision; Hamas said it deepened the division. The elections called for within six months were not held.

law_name: Presidential decree of 15 January 2021 calling legislative, presidential and PNC elections
description: Set legislative elections for 22 May 2021 and a presidential election for 31 July 2021; 93% of eligible voters registered according to the Central Elections Commission. On 29 April 2021 Abbas postponed them indefinitely, citing Israel's refusal to permit voting by Palestinians in East Jerusalem.
significance: The postponement remains one of the main criticisms of his presidency (see polemics).

law_name: Constitutional Decree No. 1 of 2024 and Constitutional Declaration No. 1 of 2025 on presidential succession; creation of the vice-presidency (2025)
description: In November 2024 Abbas decreed that the Speaker of the Palestinian National Council, Rawhi Fattouh, would act as president if the office fell vacant. In April 2025 the PLO created the post of vice-chairman of its Executive Committee, also styled vice-president of the State of Palestine, and Abbas appointed Hussein al-Sheikh. On 26 October 2025 his Constitutional Declaration No. 1 of 2025 revoked the 2024 decree and provided that, in the absence of the Legislative Council, the vice-president would act as president for up to 90 days, during which a presidential election must be held, extendable once by the PLO Central Council in case of force majeure.
significance: Replaces the Basic Law's rule that the Speaker of the Legislative Council acts as interim president; critics said it was adopted without due process (see polemics).

law_name: Decree-law of 10 February 2025 repealing the system of payments to prisoners and families of 'martyrs' and transferring social assistance to the National Economic Empowerment Institution (Tamkeen)
description: Revoked the legislation under which the PA paid stipends to Palestinians held in Israeli prisons, scaled to the length of their sentence, and to families of Palestinians killed or wounded in the conflict, including in attacks on Israelis, a system the US and Israeli governments call 'pay for slay'. Payments were moved to a needs-based welfare programme run by the Palestinian National Economic Empowerment Institution (Tamkeen). According to Axios, the decision had been negotiated with the Biden administration and was timed for the start of Trump's second term.
significance: A central reform demanded by the United States (Taylor Force Act), Israel and the EU; its implementation is disputed (see promises and polemics).

law_name: Draft Interim Constitution of the State of Palestine (drafting committee decree of 18 August 2025; draft submitted 5 February 2026)
description: By decree of 18 August 2025 Abbas created a 17-member committee chaired by legal adviser Muhammad al-Hajj Qasim to draft an interim constitution for the transition 'from the current authority to a fully-fledged state'. The committee handed him a draft of about 70 pages on 5 February 2026 after seven months and 70 meetings; he sent it to the PLO Executive Committee for review and on 9 February ordered its publication for 60 days of public comment, after which the committee is to prepare a final text for a referendum. According to The Times of Israel the draft keeps a hybrid presidential-parliamentary system, limits the president to two four-year terms and must be approved by referendum.
significance: Would replace the Basic Law, last amended in 2005. Analysts quoted by The National called the step 'largely symbolic' or doubted it would be applied; no final text or referendum date had been announced as of October 2026 in the sources found.

law_name: Amendment to the local elections law requiring candidates to accept the PLO 'national programme' (January 2026)
description: An amendment announced by the Central Elections Commission ahead of the April 2026 municipal elections requires all candidates to sign a statement accepting the PLO's 'national programme', which The Times of Israel describes as an apparent reference to PLO resolutions including recognition of Israel, renunciation of terrorism and a two-state solution. A separate decree-law of 11 January 2026 set religious seat quotas in certain municipalities.
significance: Analysts quoted by The Times of Israel said it would likely keep Hamas and similar factions out of municipal elections and could set a precedent for national elections; Hamas did not formally take part in the 25 April 2026 local elections.

law_name: Decree-law of 14 June 2026 amending Decree-Law No. 1 of 2007 on General Elections
description: Increases the Legislative Council from 132 to 200 seats, lowers the threshold to 1%, raises the minimum list size from 16 to 20 candidates, requires at least one woman among every three candidates on a list and lowers the minimum candidate age from 28 to 23. Members elected to the Legislative Council automatically become the homeland's representatives in the Palestinian National Council.
significance: Prepared the legislative elections he called for 28 November 2026 by decree of 9 July 2026, which he postponed on 10 October 2026 to 11 September 2027.

law_name: Presidential decrees calling PNC elections (1 November 2026) and legislative elections (28 November 2026), and decree of 10 October 2026 postponing legislative and presidential elections to 11 September 2027
description: In February 2026 Abbas called the first direct elections to the PLO's Palestinian National Council for 1 November 2026, at home and abroad; on 9 July 2026 he set legislative elections for 28 November 2026, and in June announced a presidential election for early 2027. On 10 October 2026 a new decree cancelled the November legislative vote and set simultaneous presidential and legislative elections for 11 September 2027, citing Israeli military operations, settlement expansion and settler violence, the withholding of PA revenues, restrictions on candidates, election staff and observers in Gaza and East Jerusalem, and the lack of progress on Gaza's reconstruction and on the international stabilisation force (WAFA, as reported by The Jerusalem Post and Al Jazeera).
significance: Would be the first national elections since 2005–2006. Whether the PNC vote of 1 November 2026 will still take place could not be confirmed from the sources found.
